mira.cs: Quick heads-up — onboarding for VerdantHealth is showing repeated latency spikes that violate the latency SLO (target p50 < 180ms) over the last 12h. We have a renewal touchpoint in 3 weeks. Need Ops confirmation on whether this will trigger SLA credits and what message we should send the customer. :eyes:

deploy-bot: [ALERT] service=verdant-inference region=us-east p50=320ms p90=890ms errors=0.18% throughput=120rps. Spike started ~11:30 UTC. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/verdant/latency (auto-snapshot).

sam.ops: Investigating — early look shows autoscaler brought some replicas down overnight and a subset of requests routed to a smaller GPU profile with higher cold-start latencies. I'm running a diff on routing logs now. ETA 30m.

mira.cs: If that pattern holds, do we expect recurring hits or is this a transient blip? Customer called out low latency in their onboarding checklist; they'd expect explanation and a remediation timeline.

sam.ops: Seems deterministic: when burst >100rps and prefix cache misses hit, routing falls back to tpu-small-pool which has different kernel paths. Two mitigation options: 1) pin Verdant route to dedicated-pool-east1 (fast, manual) or 2) tweak autoscaler policy to keep 1 warm replica (safer, needs change). I can apply (1) now.

aj.sales: Renewal context: Verdant is evaluating Dedicated. If we apply a manual pin and avoid visible errors, can we avoid issuing a formal credit? We prefer to keep customer satisfied without creating a credit precedent, but prioritize transparency.

mira.cs: We'll be transparent. If it hits the SLA formula we have to offer credit per contract. Ops - can you give a quick credit calc draft so CS can prep comms?

sam.ops: Sure. SLA credit calc (quick):
```
SLO: uptime 99.9% per 30d window OR latency p50 <= 180ms
Observed: latency breaches window = 12h over 30d -> breach_fraction = 12 / (30*24) = 0.0167
Contract: credit = min(100%, breach_fraction * 100%) * credit_multiplier
Example: 0.0167 -> ~1.67% credit of monthly invoice (subject to cap)
```
This is a rough calc — legal/tier rules may change multiplier/cap.

mira.cs: Perfect. Can you also paste the exact route command so I can include steps in the comms?

sam.ops: Command to pin (one-liner):
```
redwood route update --customer verdanthealth --route-id r-8342 --pool dedicated-pool-east1 --force
```
I'll run this if you give the green light. It should reduce p50 to ~140-160ms immediately.

linh.eng: I'll leave a trace for the rollout and add an alert suppression for the next 2h to avoid noisy paging while we stabilize. Also adding a perf regression test against their sample prompts.

mira.cs: Greenlight from CS: please proceed with pin and drop me a short before/after snapshot so I can update the customer during tomorrow's call. Also cc @aj.sales on the comm to keep renewal context aligned.

sam.ops: Running pin now. Will post snapshots in 10m. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: [ACTION] route update started by sam.ops at 2639001405. Job ID: job-9823.

sam.ops: Post-pin snapshot: p50=148ms p90=210ms errors=0.05% throughput=125rps. Looks stable. Uploading perf graph to the thread.

mira.cs: Thanks — will draft a short note: "We identified a routing/autoscaler interaction, pinned your workload to a low-latency pool, and are rolling an autoscaler policy fix. No service interruption expected; we will follow up with the formal SLO reconciliation and any credit calculation if required." Sharing to Verdant after you confirm there's no regression.

aj.sales: Thanks team. Please include proposed credit calc as an attachment in the comms (even if $0) so the customer sees we ran the math. Also flag if this should influence the Dedicated pitching conversation.

sam.ops: Will attach calc + perf graph. Recommending we offer a goodwill token (one week free trial of Dedicated) if they raise concerns during renewal — we can discuss terms.

mira.cs: Good plan. I'll schedule the customer update and include all artifacts. Closing loop once legal confirms credit policy. :lock:
